biography: Nenê Finotti, a name whispered with anticipation in Brazilian motorsport, hails from the vibrant favelas of São Paulo. His journey began not on the asphalt, but on the dusty dirt tracks of his neighborhood, where he honed his skills drifting beat-up bikes. Racing wasn't a dream initially, but a necessity – a means to escape poverty. His raw talent caught the eye of a local mechanic, Seu Jorge, who saw in Nenê a spark of greatness. Jorge mortgaged his shop to buy Nenê a kart, and the rest, as they say, is history in the making. Finotti quickly rose through the ranks, his aggressive style turning heads and ruffling feathers. Now, at 22, he pilots the Metalmoro MRX P4, a symbol of his meteoric rise and a testament to the unwavering belief of one old mechanic. His current aim is to prove he belongs at the top, showcasing his skills in every race.
drivingStyle: Finotti's driving is characterized by a fearless, almost reckless abandon. He's a late-braking specialist, often diving into corners where others wouldn't dare. Tire management isn't exactly his forte; he prefers to push from the start, relying on his raw speed and car control to compensate. Under pressure, Nenê thrives; the higher the stakes, the more aggressively he drives, often resulting in spectacular overtakes or equally spectacular crashes. He lives by the motto, 'Win or crash trying.'

rivalries.reason: A clash of generations; Esteves, the seasoned veteran, views Finotti as an undisciplined upstart, while Finotti sees Esteves as a relic of a bygone era.
A fierce on-track battle at Interlagos resulted in both drivers retiring, sparking a personal feud that plays out both on and off the circuit.
Oliveira, a more calculated driver, openly criticizes Finotti's aggressive style, labeling it dangerous and unsustainable.

quirks: Always wears the same faded São Paulo FC jersey under his racing suit.
Listens to a specific samba song ('Brasil Pandeiro') moments before entering the car.
Has a lucky charm – a small, hand-carved wooden toucan given to him by Seu Jorge – that he keeps in his helmet.
famousQuote: "Life's too short to drive slow, irmão!"
careerHighlight: Winning the Brazilian Endurance Championship junior title in 2021. It was the culmination of years of hard work and a testament to his and Seu Jorge’s sacrifices, securing him the Metalmoro drive.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead on the final lap of the 2022 Interlagos 500. The incident cost him a potential victory and severely damaged his reputation with some sponsors.
